title: 6. Internet Topology
content: ## Autonomous Systems The internet is divided into **autonomous systems** (routing domains) each of which is under the control of (and corresponds to) a single administrative entity (University, company, backbone network etc.). - Neighbouring systems will interact to coordinate routing and have business relationships. - They can be identified by 32 bit values called **AS Numbers** **Inter-domain Routing**: A network with two autonomous systems. ### AS Topology - **Node:** Autonomous System - There is a high variability in node degree ("power law") as there are only a few very highly-connected AS's while most only have a few connections - **Edge:** Two AS’s that connect to each other AS topology can be inferred by: - Mapping `traceroute` data to the AS level - Measurements of the inter-domain routing protocol These approaches are hard because data is often out of date and data collection is also difficult. - Seeing peer-peer edges is difficult. #### Business Relations within AS' **Customer Provider** - Customer needs to be reachable from everyone - The job of the provider - Customer does not want to provide a transit service - Traffic in but no traffic out **Peer-Peer Relationship** Peers exchange traffic between customers. - AS exports only customer routes to a peer - AS exports a peer’s routes only to its customers **Backbone networks** Have multiple Points-of-Presence (PoPs) with lots of communication between PoPs. They accommodate traffic demands and limit delay. - *Inter-PoP links* are long distance and high-bandwidth - *Intra-PoP links* are shorter cables that have aggregated bandwidth ## Route Propagation Provide an additional way to hierarchically aggregate routing information is a large internet. Divide the routing problem in two parts: 1. Routing within a single autonomous system (selected by an AS) 2. Routing between autonomous systems (an internet-wide standard) ### EGP and BGP: Inter-domain Routing Protocols **Exterior Gateway Protocol (EGP)** - Forced a tree-like topology onto the Internet - Did not allow for the topology to become general - Tree like structure: there is a single backbone and autonomous systems are connected only as parents and children and not as peers **Border Gateway Protocol (BGP)** - Assumes that the Internet is an arbitrarily interconnected set of ASs. - Today’s Internet consists of an interconnection of multiple backbone networks (they are usually called service provider networks, and they are operated by private companies rather than the government) - Sites are connected to each other in arbitrary ways
